t: A small open-source walking robot you can 3D print and build at home.
steps: Download the free body files from the Otto DIY site or Printables.
Print the head, body, legs, and feet with about 100 grams of plastic filament.
Gather an Arduino Nano, a Nano shield, four small servo motors, a distance sensor, a buzzer, and an AA battery holder.
Install the free Arduino IDE and add the OttoDIYLib library.
Center each servo with a test sketch before you attach the legs.
Assemble the robot and connect the wires to the shield.
Upload the basic walking example and watch Otto take its first steps.
meta: Wild Open. From $150. A few stores.
